issues.t: Automatic transmission slipping or failing
issues.sym: Revs climb but the van barely moves, shifts stop, or it suddenly won't go forward or reverse. ABS and traction control lights sometimes come on at the same time.
issues.why: The four-speed automatic shared with the Ford Freestar is this van's biggest weak spot. Torque converter and internal failures are common, often between 50,000 and 100,000 miles, and some vans failed again after repair.
issues.next: If it slips or loses drive, get off the road safely and don't keep driving it. Have the codes read and the fluid checked, and ask a Ford dealer to confirm the torque converter recall was done before paying for a rebuild.

issues.t: Torque converter can fail and cut power (recall)
issues.sym: Sudden loss of power or drive while moving, with no warning.
issues.why: Under recall 12V-006, the torque converter can fail and cause a sudden loss of power, raising the risk of a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls. If the recall is open, don't wait: have a Ford dealer do it free.

issues.t: Third-row seat anchor can rust loose (recall)
issues.sym: The third-row seat may rattle, feel loose, or not latch firmly in place.
issues.why: Under recall 13V-081, the sheet metal that holds the third-row seat latch strikers can rust through, so the seat may come unlatched in a rear crash.
issues.next: Don't seat anyone in the third row if it feels loose. Check your VIN for this recall and have it repaired free at a Ford dealer.

issues.t: Fuel connection can leak (recall)
issues.sym: A raw gasoline smell, or fuel dripping under the van.
issues.why: Recall 06E-056 covered a fuel connection that could fail and leak fuel, creating a fire risk near an ignition source.
issues.next: If you smell gasoline, don't drive the van; have it towed. Check your VIN for open recalls.

issues.t: Engine computer damaged by water leaks
issues.sym: Flickering dash lights, radio or A/C cutting out, stalling, a limp-mode speed limit, or no reverse, often during or after rain. A camshaft sensor code may appear.
issues.why: On this van and its twin, the Ford Freestar, water can get past the under-hood shield and onto the engine computer (PCM), corroding it. A new sensor alone usually doesn't fix it.
issues.next: If it acts up in rain, have the PCM area checked for water. Fix the water shield or leak at the same time as any PCM replacement, or it can come back.

issues.t: Misfire from clogged EGR ports in the intake
issues.sym: Check engine light, rough idle or shaking, especially at higher mileage.
issues.why: The small exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) passage in the intake manifold can plug with carbon sludge, so one or more cylinders run poorly. RepairPal lists it as the most common Monterey problem.
issues.next: Have the misfire codes read. Ask the shop to check the EGR ports in the intake before replacing coils or injectors.

issues.t: Misfire from a failing ignition coil pack
issues.sym: Rough running, shaking at idle, loss of power and a flashing or steady check engine light. Wet weather can make it worse.
issues.why: The 4.2L V6 uses one coil pack with plug wires. A cracked or damp coil pack, or worn plugs and wires, causes misfires.
issues.next: If the check engine light flashes, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off. Replacing plugs, wires and the coil pack together is common.

issues.t: Squealing camshaft synchronizer
issues.sym: A screech or squeal from the engine that rises with RPM. Some vans also stall at stops.
issues.why: The camshaft synchronizer, which drives the cam position sensor, wears its internal bearing. If it fails it can also leak oil.
issues.next: Have the noise pinned down with a stethoscope. Replace the synchronizer soon; a failed one can cause stalling and a no-start.

issues.t: Blower fan only works on high
issues.sym: The heater and A/C fan only blows on the highest setting; lower speeds don't work.
issues.why: On vans with manual fan controls, the blower motor resistor fails, leaving only the high-speed circuit working.
issues.next: This isn't urgent. Replace the blower resistor, and check the blower motor if it is noisy or draws too much current.

issues.t: Front wheel bearing whine or hum
issues.sym: A hum, whine or whistle from the front that changes with speed, sometimes louder when turning.
issues.why: Ford issued service bulletins for front hub bearing noise on these vans. Worn bearings get louder over time.
issues.next: Have the front hubs checked for play. Replace a noisy bearing before it gets loose, which can affect steering and the ABS sensor.

issues.t: ABS and traction control lights on
issues.sym: The ABS and traction control lights come on or flicker; cruise control may stop working too.
issues.why: Ford bulletins for these years cover ABS module calibration faults and related warning-light codes. Some vans need a new ABS/traction control module.
issues.next: Normal braking usually still works, but ABS and traction control may be off. Drive carefully on slippery roads and have the codes read soon.

issues.t: Rear brakes wear fast or calipers seize
issues.sym: Grinding or squealing from the rear, a pulling or dragging feel, or rear pads wearing out much sooner than expected.
issues.why: Ford issued bulletins for fast rear brake wear on these vans, and owners report seized rear calipers.
issues.next: Have the rear brakes checked at every oil change. Replace seized calipers along with pads and rotors, and flush old brake fluid.

issues.t: Power sliding door or liftgate will not open
issues.sym: A power sliding door or the power liftgate stops working, beeps, or only opens by hand.
issues.why: Ford bulletins cover power sliding door and liftgate faults on these vans, including a stored C1999 code.
issues.next: Make sure the child lock and door switches are set correctly, then have the codes read. A dealer may be able to reset or reprogram the system before replacing parts.

issues.t: Power liftgate can drop suddenly (recall)
issues.sym: The open power liftgate may drift down or fall without warning.
issues.why: Under recall 06V-069, a liftgate strut could fail and let the liftgate drop on someone standing under it.
issues.next: Don't stand under an open liftgate until the recall is confirmed done. Check your VIN and have the repair done free.

issues.t: Cracked wheel hubs or rotors (recall)
issues.sym: Grinding, vibration or a clunk from a wheel.
issues.why: Under recall 04V-446, hubs, rotors or wheel bearings could crack and, in the worst case, a wheel could separate.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. Any new grinding or clunk from a wheel needs inspection right away.

issues.t: Power steering line can come loose (recall)
issues.sym: Power steering fluid leaking, harder steering, or smoke from under the hood.
issues.why: Under recall 03V-457, a power steering line could disconnect and spray fluid onto the hot exhaust, causing smoke or fire.
issues.next: If you see smoke, pull over and turn off the engine. Check your VIN for this recall.

issues.t: Alternator stops charging
issues.sym: Battery light on, dim lights, a dead battery, or the van stalling.
issues.why: The alternator is one of the most common repairs reported on these vans past about 100,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the charging system tested before buying a new battery. If the battery light comes on while driving, head straight to a shop.

issues.t: A/C compressor fails
issues.sym: The A/C blows warm, the compressor clutch doesn't engage, or there is a grinding noise with the A/C on.
issues.why: Owners report A/C compressor replacements, sometimes after the compressor belt broke.
issues.next: Have the A/C pressures and clutch checked. If a compressor fails internally, the system should be flushed and the drier replaced too.

issues.t: Power steering leak or hard steering
issues.sym: Whining while turning, fluid spots under the front, or steering that feels heavy or slow to return to center.
issues.why: Owners report power steering pump leaks and, in some cases, pump and steering rack replacement.
issues.next: Check the power steering fluid level. If it keeps dropping or steering gets heavy, have the pump, hoses and rack inspected.

issues.t: Broken outer CV joint
issues.sym: Clicking when turning sharply, or a clunk when pulling away.
issues.why: Ford bulletin 0598 covers broken outer CV joints on vans built before May 1, 2005.
issues.next: Have the front axles inspected. A clicking CV joint should be replaced before it breaks and leaves you stranded.

issues.t: Message center dim or blank
issues.sym: The message center in the dash is too dim to read in daylight, or goes blank, so you can't see mileage or door-ajar warnings.
issues.why: The instrument cluster develops faults with age; owners point to bad solder joints. Ford also issued cluster code bulletins for these vans.
issues.next: Have the cluster tested. A cluster repair service is often cheaper than a new unit.

issues.t: Rear defroster and antenna stop working
issues.sym: The rear window defroster doesn't clear the glass, and radio reception gets poor.
issues.why: The rear window grid doubles as the radio antenna. Ford bulletins cover broken grid lines and loose terminal tabs on these vans.
issues.next: A shop can reattach the terminal tab or repair the grid lines with a kit.

issues.t: Front power windows stop working
issues.sym: A front window won't go up or down, or works only sometimes.
issues.why: Ford issued a bulletin for front window motors not working on these vans.
issues.next: If a window is stuck open, cover it before rain. Have the switch and motor tested.
